title: Keyboard remapping doesn't working in powershell and other windows tools
author: ronald-wentworth
summary: A CapsLock/Ctrl/Alt remap fails in Task Manager and an unspecified PowerShell surface, but those targets may involve different executables and privilege boundaries.

confidence.rationale: The canonical Task Manager issue is confirmed; the exact PowerShell host is the decisive missing fact.

judgment.rationale: Task Manager has a canonical reproducible issue, while 'PowerShell' could mean Console Host, Windows Terminal, PowerShell ISE, or an elevated process. The unresolved portion cannot be assigned safely without that distinction.
evidence: The report uses PowerToys 0.90.1 and says the same remap stops in Task Manager, Device Manager, and PowerShell.
Issue 27568 separately tracks and reproduces remaps failing in Task Manager.
The latest comment asks which exact PowerShell program is meant; no answer is present.
judgment.recommended_action: Link the Task Manager symptom to issue 27568 and request the exact PowerShell executable/elevation context for the remaining behavior.

fix_assessment.rationale: The Task Manager portion is already tracked by issue 27568, and the remaining host/elevation context is not specific enough for a new fix.

issue_context.summary: A CapsLock/Ctrl/Alt remap fails in Task Manager and an unspecified PowerShell surface, but those targets may involve different executables and privilege boundaries.
known_information: The mapping cycles Caps Lock to Ctrl, Ctrl to Alt, and Alt to Caps Lock.
Several named Windows tools may run at a different integrity level from PowerToys.
No diagnostic archive or current-version confirmation is supplied.
inferences: The Windows-tool failures may be the known integrity-level behavior, while the PowerShell failure may depend on which host launches it.
issue_context.analysis: Treating all named targets as one defect would conflate a known Task Manager case with an unspecified terminal host. Exact executable and elevation observations are needed before proposing engine changes.
initial_investigation: Read the full report, both comments, labels, and similar-issue references.
Inspected issue 27568 and confirmed it remains open with Status-Reproducible for Task Manager.

information_gaps.information: The exact PowerShell surface and executable that ignores the remap.
information_gaps.why_needed: Separates Windows Terminal, conhost, PowerShell ISE, and pwsh process-target behavior.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Name the application shown in Task Manager Details, such as WindowsTerminal.exe, conhost.exe, powershell.exe, or pwsh.exe.

information_gaps.information: Whether PowerToys and each affected tool are running elevated under the same Windows user.
information_gaps.why_needed: Tests the known integrity-level boundary for global keyboard hooks.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Record PowerToys elevation state and whether each affected window was launched as administrator.

information_gaps.information: Whether the non-Task-Manager symptom reproduces on the current stable release.
information_gaps.why_needed: Avoids designing against behavior from 0.90.1 that may have changed.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Retest on the current stable release and provide the About version.

actions.label: Confirm PowerShell host and elevation

comment.body:
Thanks for listing the remap and the affected Windows tools. Task Manager behavior is already tracked in #27568, but the PowerShell portion may be a different path. Please provide.

1. The exact PowerShell host/executable (for example WindowsTerminal.exe, conhost.exe, powershell.exe, pwsh.exe, or PowerShell ISE).
2. Whether PowerToys and that host are each running as administrator under the same Windows user.
3. Whether the non-Task-Manager failure still reproduces on the current stable PowerToys release.

This will determine whether the remaining issue is the known integrity-level boundary or a separate terminal-host remapping defect.
